The function above is a standard merge implementation. It uses two pointers (i and j) to traverse both lists simultaneously. At each step, it compares the current elements of both lists and appends the smaller one to the result, then moves the corresponding pointer forward. Once one list is exhausted, it appends all remaining elements of the other list.

This approach works because both input lists are already sorted. The time complexity is O(n + m) where n and m are the lengths of the two lists, and the space complexity is O(n + m) for the result list.

The function does not use sorted() or .
